claims.claim: The three Lab front ends share one exact Python governor; their agreement is transport and replay interoperability, not independent algorithm validation.
limitations: Finite rational weighted graph semantics depend on supplied carrier, weights, claims and proposals. No empirical source-truth detector or cross-language mathematical engine is provided.

claims.claim: Lab tests supply bounded checks of weighted L1 obstruction, gauge invariance, component sums, CUT descent and exact replay, with explicit counterexamples to globally monotone histories.
limitations: Generated tests do not prove all admitted graphs or all rationals. Differential tests currently fail setup. RETRACT can increase D; ASSERT monotonicity is optional; D and Phi_1 are not interchangeable.

claims.claim: Resource checks bound admitted graph/move/text sizes and each obstruction enumeration, but they do not prove an end-to-end memory, total session cost or latency ceiling.
limitations: RPC reads full lines before admission cap; C# queue wait precedes per-exchange timeout; no independent bit-complexity or wall-clock proof.

claims.claim: Receipt SHA and current-core replay detect tested tampering; they do not establish historical code-version authenticity, author identity or semantic adequacy.

claims.claim: PrimitiveDifference proves quotient factorization exactly when the supplied operation or invariant respects the supplied zero-equivalence relation, and explicitly exhibits failure without congruence.
dependencies: zero equivalence laws supplied in structure

claims.claim: ShadowBoundary formalizes information-preservation requirements: equal observations cannot decode distinct targets, and an augmentation must separate every relevant target collision.
limitations: Generic theorem has no finiteness premise despite file label. Bool/Unit examples do not establish collisions in an actual runtime unless correspondence is shown. Target-augmented success assumes access to the target. No cost, computable discovery or approximate accuracy claim.

findings.title: Valid computed Python rationals are rejected by the C# client
findings.counterexample: Two vertices, one edge weight1000, ASSERT value consisting of64 nines. Python admits scenario, computes67-character defect, and verifies its receipt; current compiled C# Receipt.Validate throws Protocol for defect_after.
findings.impact: Desktop RunAsync rejects a valid core result and cannot display/save that run; identical admitted scenario works through Python.
findings.next_action: Separate input rational admission cap from bounded canonical computed-output parsing; prove/derive a safe output bound or use transport-size limits, and add cross-language arithmetic-growth regression.

findings.title: Differential oracle fixture references the pre-migration paper path
findings.counterexample: Both tests in test_differential.py error at fixture setup; old papers/005... does not exist, relocated papers/pfp/005... does.
findings.impact: Current suite cannot exercise its advertised independent port-oracle comparison. Historical scores saying it passes are not fresh evidence.
findings.next_action: Repair the scoped fixture path and pin source custody, then rerun bounded differential checks.

findings.title: DTO validation accepts a nonhex digest while claiming a mirrored wire contract
findings.counterexample: Receipt.Validate accepts Digest=new string(z,64); Python ReceiptOut requires lowercase hex. Field-name schema test misses this constraint.
findings.impact: Malformed core responses can be admitted locally. This is not a successful bypass of Python verify_receipt. Other DTO checks also omit status enums and full scenario validation.
findings.next_action: Enforce actual wire constraints at the client boundary and add adversarial shape/enum/hash tests; qualify schema correspondence claims.

findings.title: The web chart labels attempted and mixed metrics as defect after each step
findings.counterexample: Paper005 refused relational CUT reports attempted Phi_1 5 while unchanged section D remains6 and unchanged Phi_1 remains3; chart plots5 under Defect after each step. ASSERT points use D, claim-CUT points use Phi_1.
findings.impact: Visualization can imply a state trajectory or monotonicity property that the receipt does not represent. Table shows refusal status, but chart label does not identify attempted metric.
findings.next_action: Label metric and proposed/admitted values explicitly or generate separate actual-state D/Phi_1 traces from replay.

findings.title: README desktop command invokes a nonexistent package entry point
findings.counterexample: python -m pfp_lab stdio exits1: no pfp_lab.__main__. Actual client correctly invokes pfp_lab.cli.main.
findings.impact: Manual setup/troubleshooting command fails; installed client path is unaffected.
findings.next_action: Correct documentation to the owned CLI module.
